transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net fault management, my name is Kieran. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Kieran, I'm calling about my eighty-four year old mother's landline and broadband. There is terrible static on the line and her emergency care alarm has stopped connecting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can check the line for faults today, Soraya. Can you provide the account telephone number and your mother's date of birth for identity confirmation?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The landline number is 0141 496 0882, and my mother's date of birth is the fourteenth of March 1942.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that locates the account record on our Essential Landline and Broadband package. What is the current status of the equipment?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Whenever you pick up the handset there is a deafening hiss and crackle, and her red care alarm box on the wall is flashing red and beeping error code two.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what is happening is that severe static and line noise on the landline is preventing your mother's emergency care alarm from communicating, while also causing intermittent broadband drops. Have I understood the problem accurately, Soraya?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly! It started yesterday during the heavy rain and it hasn't stopped since.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me see if the line test detects a battery cross or loop resistance fault on the circuit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please, I am desperately worried about her! She lives alone and had a bad fall last month. If she slips again and that pendant alarm can't dial through to the warden, she could be lying on the floor for hours! This is an absolute emergency!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We have mandatory diagnostic procedures that must be executed at the master socket before an engineer can be scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you not just test the line from your computer right now without putting an eighty-four year old woman through this?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An automated line test cannot distinguish between external cable faults and damaged customer internal wiring without isolation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, what do I need to do? I am at her bungalow right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Locate the main master telephone socket on the wall where the telephone line enters the house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm standing by the socket in the hallway near the coat rack.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the socket have a horizontal split across the front faceplate with two small screws, or is it a single moulded plastic block?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's an NTE5 socket with two screws and S-Net Openreach printed in the corner.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there an ADSL microfilter plugged into that socket, or does the master plate have dual sockets for phone and broadband?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, there is a small white rectangular microfilter box plugged in, with one lead going to the router and the other going to the care alarm base unit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unplug that microfilter completely from the wall socket, along with both telephone cables attached to it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unplugging it now... okay, it's unplugged, both the black telephone wire and the grey DSL lead are out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you have a spare microfilter available in the property to swap in, or another telephone handset in a bedroom?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, we only have the one filter that S-Net supplied when the service was installed three years ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now take a small Phillips screwdriver and remove the two retaining screws on the lower detachable half of the master socket faceplate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, you want me to unscrew the wall socket? I am a retired school teacher, not a telecoms technician! Why do I have to take the wall apart?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Removing the faceplate exposes the test socket behind it, which disconnects all internal bell wires and extensions throughout the bungalow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me find a screwdriver in her kitchen drawer... hold on. Okay, loosening the two screws now... pulling the bottom plate off gently.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you see a hidden telephone jack socket on the right hand side behind that plastic plate, and are any bell wires touching?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, there is another socket hidden behind the faceplate, and there are two thin orange and white wires screwed into the back terminals.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Plug a corded telephone handset directly into that test socket without any microfilters or splitters attached.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Plugging the phone handset in now. Putting the receiver directly to my ear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Listen to the dial tone and tell me if the loud static crackle is still audible, or if the line is quiet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, did you want me to plug the care alarm or the telephone handset into the test socket? You said telephone earlier.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you'd pay attention to what I'm asking we wouldn't be wasting time here. I explicitly stated the corded telephone handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is no need to be rude and condescending! I am trying my best to help my elderly mother while you speak to me with complete contempt!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating the instruction clearly. What do you hear on the receiver?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The static is still deafening. It sounds like rushing water and frying bacon. I can barely hear the dial tone underneath it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now dial 17070 on the keypad to access the automated quiet line test facility, and press option two when prompted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dialling 17070... pressing option two for quiet line... the crackle is just as loud and continuous, like electricity sizzling.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The quiet line test confirms high resistance audio interference and conductive leakage on the physical copper pair outside the property boundary.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right! So it is a problem with the line outside the house, exactly like I told you forty minutes ago! Can you book an emergency engineer right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look, the physical copper line from the telegraph pole belongs to Openreach, not S-Net, so you'll have to get in touch with Openreach yourself to fix the line static.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What? Openreach does not take calls from retail customers, you are our provider! You have to report the fault to them directly through your wholesale portal!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated portal can only log standard four-day appointment requests for residential copper lines without priority care escalation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Four days? Her emergency care alarm is dead! If she has a medical emergency over the weekend, what is she supposed to do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You would have to arrange private supervisory family care until Openreach clears the line defect in your local area.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is utterly disgraceful. You are washing your hands of a vulnerable pensioner's safety.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating company policy on non-commercial PSTN maintenance timelines.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you going to submit the engineer ticket or not?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have submitted ticket reference LN-40281 into the automated Openreach dispatch pool.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And is the line working now? No! The alarm is still beeping and the static is still there. Nothing is resolved at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The physical line fault requires roadside intervention, so it cannot clear remotely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am lodging an emergency complaint with the health authority and your head office.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding this fault record today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, you've been completely useless.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net fault management.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for ringing S-Net today, have a good one Soraya. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
